text:
A: Hello! Oh, sorry, I think I was on mute. Can you hear me now?
B: Yeah, I can hear you.
A: Brilliant. I'm Karen. Sorry, I've still got my work lanyard on, I've literally just walked in.
B: That's fine. I'm Ioana.
A: Ioana. Lovely name. Where are you, then?
B: Burnt Oak. North West London.
A: Oh, not far from me, sort of. I'm Basingstoke. Well, it's not that close, is it, to be honest, it's the M3 and then a nightmare.
B: Yeah, it's a way.
A: What do you do? Is that all right to ask? I'm not sure what we're meant to talk about.
B: I think it's whatever. Erm, I'm a lettings administrator. At an estate agent's in Edgware.
A: Oh, so tenancies and that?
B: Yeah, tenancy agreements, deposits, gas safety reminders, chasing references. Landlord statements. Basically making sure nobody gets fined.
A: That sounds really organised. I'm admin as well, at a building maintenance firm. I book the engineers in, chase invoices, answer the phones. But I'm hopeless, to be fair. My desk is just Post-it notes. I double-booked a plumber last month and he turned up at a job where someone else was already under the sink.
B: [laughs] Okay, that's quite bad.
A: It was bad! I owned up, though. My manager just sort of sighed.
B: Honestly, owning up is half of it. The negotiators at mine promise tenants stuff without checking, then it's me who has to sort it. They never say sorry.
A: That would wind me up, yeah.
B: It does. I've been told to soften my emails, so.
A: [laughs] Soften them how?
B: Like, I wrote to a landlord, "As I said in my previous three emails." And apparently that's passive-aggressive.
A: Well, it's a bit aggressive. But he deserved it, probably.
B: He did. He emails me at eleven at night.
A: Oh, no. Sorry, where was I? I was going to ask, what do you do when you're not at work? That's probably a boring question, isn't it?
B: No, it's fine. Erm, walking, mostly, at the weekends. Stanmore Common. And I'm doing an accounting course in the evenings, AAT.
A: In the evenings? After a full day? I'd be asleep on the settee by eight. I'm knackered most nights, I just put a crime drama on.
B: What are you watching?
A: Oh, I'm halfway through this new one, the detective with the dodgy back, I can't remember the name. I binged four episodes Sunday while my son was at his dad's.
B: I watch loads of those. Scandinavian ones especially. My boyfriend talks through them, so I watch them on my own.
A: Callum does that! My son, he's fourteen. "Who's that? Is he the killer?" Every five minutes.
B: Yeah, that's Liam. And then he guesses right and he's so smug about it.
A: [laughs] Have you seen The Bridge?
B: Yeah, the first two series are really good. Then it kind of goes off.
A: I never finished it. I don't really finish anything, to be honest. My mum gives me books and they just sit there.
B: I read on the bus. The 113's always late, so I get loads done.
A: Every cloud, eh?
